thread:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about adding per-tenant slab tags + a tiny prefetch budget to reduce fragmentation during offload. TL;DR: tag hot allocations by tenant/usage class, evict slightly older cold slabs first, and allow tenant-level prefetch budget to prevent spike tail latency. Thoughts?

 dan: Interesting. How do tags interact with eviction order? do we need per-slab LRU or a bloom-based hotset?

 mira: My thought: keep current lease/age metadata on allocations, add a small 8-bit tag field per slab (tenant id hashed + class). Evict ordering: prefer slabs with cold lease and tag mismatch to incoming tenant. That reduces cross-tenant contamination.

 kevin: Would that increase allocator overhead? adding tag checks in hot path could cost us. Could be done only in sampling/evictor path, not alloc fastpath.

 mira: Agreed. Plan: no tag checks in alloc fastpath; tags written on free/compact. Evictor/sampler will consult tags. Also proposal for tenant prefetch config:

 ```
 {"tenant_prefetch_budget": 4, "max_prefetch_bytes": 16777216, "slab_tagging": true}
 ```

 kevin: Makes sense. What about offload/paging? if a slab is offloaded to host, keep tag metadata with page header so reinstall knows tenant affinity.

 sre-ops: Also consider telemetry: track per-tenant fragmentation delta pre/post compaction. We need to expose time-series for alerts.

 mira: Yep, intend to add metrics: tenant.fragmentation_pct, tenant.prefetch_bytes, slab.tag_mismatch_evictions

 infra-bot: deploy queued: evictor-v2 -> staging (canary 10%) :rocket:

 dan: Cool. I'll throw together a microbenchmark to measure alloc fastpath cost and eviction throughput. Ping me if you want the prototype in runtime-sim.

 mira: Thanks — will post RFC draft by EOD with diagrams and compaction tradeoffs. :thumbsup:
